Bangladesh shows war crimes trial standards
2014-12-10T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/bangladesh-shows-war-crimes-trial-standards-54578

Ripping into the international communities, National Human Rights Commission Chairman Prof Mizanur Rahman yesterday said the International Crimes Tribunal of Bangladesh had set the standards of how to try war criminals transparently.

"You raise questions about the standards...but we have set standards through the fairest of trials of war criminals with the laws of the land, which didn't happen anywhere including Nuremberg, Yugoslavia, Cambodia, and Rwanda," he told a roundtable in the capital's Jatiya Press Club.

The Association for Law Research and Human Rights (ALERT) organised the roundtable on "Worldwide Violation of Human Rights and its Remedies".

Mizanur likened the international communities' criticism of Bangladesh's human rights situation to "shedding crocodile tears", saying that on one hand, they were issuing statements on the rights situation and on the other, were killing thousands of innocent women and children by drone attacks.

Their views are not acceptable, he said.

Prosecutor Rana Dasgupta said the minorities faced human rights violation due to communal politics, religious zealots, fundamentalism, and undemocratic practice by the state. The minority population is shrinking gradually through forced migration and widespread and systematic attacks on them, he alleged.

Describing Bangladesh's human rights situation as much better than other countries', former vice chancellor of National University Dr Durgadas Bhattacharyya said the situation however would deteriorate if anti-liberation forces were sheltered in politics continuously.

ALERT president Jahangir Alam Khan was in the chair.
